title: Recent Progress for Single-Molecule Magnets Based on Rare Earth Elements
claim: Even the best Ln-SMMs in this review remain far from room-temperature operation, so practical molecular memory is still blocked despite Ueff and TB gains.
explanation: The authors call Ueff the main performance metric because its height sets TB, the temperature below which thermal energy cannot reverse the moment over the barrier and magnetization is retained. They note that moving TB from 60 K to 80 K is encouraging but still far from 300 K, which they call a principal obstacle to application. Conventional magnets are separately said to be limited by the superparamagnetic effect, which molecular magnets can in principle avoid because of their fixed nanoscale size.
scope: Application prospects of high-performance Ln-SMMs, especially Tb/Dy systems.
conditions: TB here is the temperature below which the moment is blocked after the applied field is removed.
caveats: 80 K is not presented as a thermodynamic ceiling, only as the leading experimental mark in the cited work, still well below room temperature.
